questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between MapLike<K, V> and HashMap<K, V>?
choices: MapLike is the abstract data type; HashMap is one implementation of it
MapLike is a faster version of HashMap
HashMap is the abstract data type; MapLike is one implementation of it
They are two names for the same thing
questions.explanation: An interface states the contract. HashMap delivers it with buckets; TreeMap will deliver it with a BST.

questions.prompt: Why must a map's hash function be deterministic?
choices: So that get looks in the same bucket that set used
So that the map iterates in insertion order
So that resizing is never needed
questions.explanation: If the same key hashed differently on different calls, lookups would search the wrong bucket.

questions.prompt: Every key hashes to bucket 0. What is the cost of get on a map holding n entries?
questions.explanation: One bucket holds all n entries, so get scans a list of length n.

questions.prompt: Every key hashes to bucket 0. What is the total cost of inserting n distinct keys?
questions.explanation: Each set scans the bucket for the key first: 0 + 1 + … + (n−1), which is O(n²).

questions.prompt: After doubling the bucket array, why can't you copy each old bucket to the same index in the new array?
choices: The new array is too small
hash(key) % capacity changes when capacity changes, so keys would be in the wrong bucket
Arrays can't be copied in TypeScript
questions.explanation: The bucket index depends on capacity, so every entry has to be rehashed.

questions.prompt: A single resize is O(n). Why is insert still O(1) amortized when capacity doubles?
choices: Resizes are skipped when the hash is good
The copies across all resizes form a geometric series that sums to less than 2n
Resizing happens on a background thread
Because the load factor is below 1
questions.explanation: Copying 6 + 12 + 24 + … up to n entries totals under 2n, so n inserts cost O(n) overall.

questions.prompt: What happens to n inserts if capacity grows by a constant 8 buckets instead of doubling?
questions.explanation: A resize every 8 inserts, each copying everything so far: about n²/16 copies.

questions.prompt: You need to group words that are anagrams of each other. Which key works?
choices: The set of distinct letters in the word
questions.explanation: Sorted letters are identical exactly for anagrams. Distinct letters fail on 'aab' vs 'abb'.

questions.prompt: For pair-sum in one pass, what do you store in the map as you walk the array?
choices: Each value → its index, then look up target − value
Each index → its value, then look up target
questions.explanation: Looking up the complement among values already seen finds the partner in O(1).

questions.prompt: Longest consecutive run: why is the 'count up from each run start' approach O(n), not O(n²)?
choices: Because the input is sorted first
Because you only count up from x when x − 1 is absent, so each number is visited by one run
Because runs are short on average
questions.explanation: Only run starts begin a count, and runs don't overlap, so the inner loop totals n steps.

questions.prompt: You insert 'Bulbasaur', 'Charmander', 'Squirtle' into your HashMap and iterate. What order do you get?
choices: Bucket order, which depends on hashes and capacity
questions.explanation: Separate chaining iterates bucket by bucket. JS's built-in Map keeps insertion order; that's not part of the ADT.
